- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true over 3–5 periods, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 10% above true for 2+ consecutive days, assume model is overfitting; apply downward bias correction.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; align forecast with sentiment trend average over last 5–7 days.
